Report Details

Violation Code: 78a86 - CASING AND CEMENTING - DEFECTIVE CASING OR CEMENTING - Operator failed to report defect in a well that has defective, insufficient or improperly cemented casing to the Department within 24 hours of discovery. Violation ID: 8226796
Permit API: 115-20351
Unconventional: Yes
County: Susquehanna
Municipality: Auburn Township
Inspection Type: Routine/Partial Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/24/2025
Comments: On site today to witness the beginning of the Koromlan 1H, 4H, 6H and 107HC (72 hr.) Pressure Build Up Tests (PBUTs). Upon arrival all (4) wells were in automated production with all annuli open and venting. Creston Consultants reps. (Jason Rajon and Ryan Carmody) were on site to perform pressure checks with a Cristal digital pressure gauge and gas screenings with a Bascom Turner Gas Explorer. Creston Consultant Reps. collected gas samples off annuli, where present, and will send out for isotopic analysis. The results will be shared with the Dept. Creston Consultants reps. (Jason Rajon and Ryan Carmody) were on site to perform flow checks with an Alicat 0-20 SLPM flow meter and gas screenings with a Bascom Turner Gas Explorer of all annuli before the start of the PBUTs. The results of the gas screenings and flow checks for each well are listed below: - If the flow test showed flow under 0.02 SLPM, a balloon was placed over open vent pipe for 10 minutes to check for any inflation of ballon indicating small amount of flow. - 1H - (13x9) annulus: under 0.02 Cu/ft per day(no balloon inflation); 25% gas initially, 5% gas peak and 5% gas sustained (9x5) annulus: under 0.02 Cu/ft per day(no balloon inflation); 45% gas initially, 10% peak and 10% gas sustained. - 4H - (20x13) annulus: 8.8 Cu/ft per day; 28% gas initially, 10% gas peak and 10% gas sustained. (13x9) annulus: 1.1 Cu/ft per day; 14% gas initially, 6% gas peak and 5% gas sustained (30sec.). (9x5) annulus: under 0.02 Cu/ft per day(no balloon inflation; 26% gas initially, 21,020 ppm peak and 20,000 ppm gas sustained (30 sec.) - 6H - (13x9) annulus: 4.8 Cu/ft per day; 18% gas initially, 13% gas peak and 13% gas sustained. (9x5) annulus: 1.9 Cu/ft per day; 29% gas initially, 11% peak and 10% gas sustained - 107HC - (20x13) annulus: under Cu/ft per day(no ballon inflation); 20 ppm gas initially, 0 ppm gas peak and 0 ppm gas sustained. (13x9) annulus: under 0.02 Cu/ft per day(no ballon inflation); 160 ppm gas initially, 0 ppm gas peak and 0 ppm gas sustained. (9x5) annulus: 1.7 Cu/ft per day; 55% gas initially, 16,080 ppm gas peak and 14,000 ppm gas sustained (30sec.). - All annuli were shut in at 12:30pm (3/24/25) with the exception of the 4H (20x13) annulus which will be shut in on Wed. (3/26/25) resulting in a 24hr. test for this annulus.

Unconventional: Yes

Comments: On June 24, 2022, DEP received a spill notification (CTS 365059) from Range Resources Kirby Steck that about 20 gallons of production fluid was spilled outside of containment at the Ogontz 3H, 7-9 Well Pad. DEP representative Brad Kline spoke with Mr. Steck on the phone around 1420 on June 24 and Mr. Steck said Range Resources was in the process of bringing a new plugging rig onsite. In the process of bringing the rig onsite, contractors were cleaning up the workspace and were vacuuming up the containment. The hose from the vacuum truck was not completely evacuated and the vacuum was turned off allowing about 20 gallons of remaining production fluid in the hose to spill outside of containment onto the well pad surface. Mr. Steck said that Range Resources contractors immediately began to scrape the pad surface to remove the impacted stone from the area. The area of impact appeared to be about 15 feet by 15 feet from the pictures provided by Mr. Steck. Mr. Steck said 2.5 inches of pad surface had to be scraped to remove to impacted soil. The impacted soil was loaded into roll off dumpsters to be removed from the site. The spill of production fluid outside of containment to the pad surface is a violation of Clean Streams Law 402(b), Chapter 78a56(a), and Solid Waste Management Act 301. Since the spill was cleaned up immediately the violations are considered corrected.

Comments: On May 1, 2023, I conducted an inspection of the Proffitt 1 well in Derry Township, Westmoreland County. At the time of inspection, the well appeared to drilled, however the well did not appear to be equipped for production. The production line from the well did not appear to be connected to a production unit or other visual production apparatus. The pump jack did not appeared to be operational. The well tag did not appear to match the correct operator information, however the API number appeared to be correct. I observed a significant amount of fluid emanating from the well. I screened the fluid, which appeared to be consisted with fluid produced by a coal bed methane well. The release did not appear to be negatively impacting near by aquatic life, ie tadpoles. Prior to leaving the location, I contacted Apollo Resources Representative Jesse Colangelo to inform him of the release. I recommended that the Operator take immediate action to correct the condition creating the release. Mr. Colangelo indicated that they would sent someone out to correct the leak. I requested photos of the repair once the release was corrected. Violations are being issued for the failure to properly control production fluid resulting in a release to the ground. The Department requests clarification as to what caused the release, the quantity of fluid released and how this was determined, how long it is believed the release was occurring. Please include the clarification information within the NOV response.

properties.content:
Report Details

Comments: On 5/8/2025, DEP representative John Rogers conducted a drilling inspection at the Seneca Resource's Taft 851 well site located in Middlebury Township, Tioga County. It was 50 degrees and overcast when I arrived on location. Upon my arrival, I first inspected the original south pad for the Taft 851 1V well. A plugged well monument is installed above the well with a plugged date of 3/24/2025. All servicing equipment has been removed from this pad. I was unaccompanied when inspecting the north pad. There are five newly drilled and completed wells on site that were staged for production. Two sand separators were attached to each wellhead, the sand separators all connected to one gas-buster style frac tank. Two produced water tanks and five GPUs have been installed on site, all staged in secondary containment. Secondary containment remains installed around the wellheads. Patterson drilling rig #805 has been mobilized to the site to drill an additional eight wells at the site. The rig was towered up on the first well, the 206HU, and had started drilling on 4/30/2025. Secondary containment has been installed for drilling operations. Nine frac tanks, diesel tanks, and chemicals were staged in secondary containment. Drill cuttings were being collected, solidified and temporarily stored in 6 dumpsters. 28 frac tanks remain staged in secondary containment on the west side of the location. I did witness a 30' x 2.5' x4" deep liquid puddle east of center pad outfall that field tested at 5.58 mS conductance. A white substance was observed in the bottom of the liquid. I collected sample 9551178 from this puddle. Liquid flowing from the center pad outfall and into the sediment basin field tested at 4.82 mS conductance. I collected sample 9551-179 from this area. I collected sample 9551-180 from soil in the bottom of the basin near the north-central pad outlet; the soil field tested at 2.414 mS conductance. Water in the sediment basin field tested at 2.10 mS conductance. I collected sample 9551181 near the east sediment basin overflow weir.Water flowing past the compost filter sock below the sediment basin field tested at 1.717 mS conductance. This water flows past the site LOD. I collected sample 9551182 from this area.After the inspection, I discussed the elevated conductance and sample collection with Seneca's Carlos Martinez.Vegetation is established in recently constructed areas. Three sediment traps and one sediment basin have been installed on site and along the access road. They have not been converted to PCSM BMPs yet. Sediment trap 3 and the sediment basin did have standing water. Temporary compost filter socks remain installed throughout the site. Violations are still outstanding for inspection ID 3846665 and ID 3855651 for puddles of water with elevated conductance discovered on the pad surface and in the sediment basin during completion operations.The DEP recommends that Seneca continues to monitor the conditions on the pad surface and the sediment basin and remove elevated conductance fluids and soils as discovered. Prevent elevated conductance fluids from leaving the facility and causing pollution to the waters of the Commonwealth. I left the site at 1215 hours.

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/27/2025
Comments: Incident Inspection of Repsol's "Broadleaf Holdings" Marcellus well site. Tory Rogers called the DEP on Friday morning May 23, 2025 to report a release of approximately 9 gallons of diesel based drilling mud released from a flare stack to the pad surface that morning. I met with Tory Rogers, Jim Brown, Megan DePue (all 3 Repsol), and Scotty Brown (DEP, OGI) on site. While drilling a future Marcellus Shale well there was a control issue, so they lit the flare stack to burn off natural gas incurred. Some drilling mud blew out of the flare stack, estimated at 7 gallons onto pad containment, and 9 gallons on the pad surface. Rogers showed us where the flare stack released drilling mud. Resource Environmental directed excavation to remove pad material the drilling mud impacted, which was approximately a 10'X60' area. They completed the cleanup around 1600 hrs the same day the release occurred. The material is in 2 dumpsters on the NE corner of the pad. I got a 1.5 ppm reading with a 10.6 eV MiniRae photoionization detector (PID) from the removed pad material, and a 0.0 ppm PID reading from the remediated pad surface, which indicates the cleanup sufficiently removed the impacted pad material. Drill cuttings in a dumpster near the drill rig gave a 135.7 ppm reading. Violations cited to the 015-23893 drilling permit are considered immediately corrected.Rogers explained they increased the density of the drill mud from 12.8 lbs/gal to 13.5 lbs/gal to provide more well control.Repsol laid the containment on this pad on February 26 thru March 3, 2025. Comments: On 07/15/2025, a Drilling inspection was conducted at the MINGO WELL SITE in Union Township, Washington County. The Department received a SPUD notification on 06/26/2025 for 15H well (125- 29184). Falcon 25 drilling crew onsite. I was accompanied by EQT drilling site manager Ezekiel. The following was observed during inspection:-The Act 9 sign was present at the site entrance. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP) andPreparedness, Prevention, and Contingency (PPC) plan was present in mailbox (Photo 1).-The well site entrance and access road appeared to be stabilized with no accelerated erosion and sedimentation issues observed (Photo 2 and 3).-I observed active construction for NINFS004 pipeline along the Mingo limit of disturbance (LOD).Overall, well pad slope and sound wall appeared to be in stable condition (Photo 4 and 5).-Secondary containment was observed throughout well site. Falcon 25 drilling rig, well casings, equipment, drill cuttings were observed within containment. Trucks were onsite to remove impaired water (Photo 6-18).-I observed multiple wet spots along the west side of the drilling secondary containment and throughout the travel lane. I utilized a Field Scout Conductivity probe to observe numerous elevated and over range readings within a 180x70 ft section. The Department contacted Environmental EQT Logan Dominick to notify them of the spill found. The elevated conductivity reading of Over range, 5.46 mS/cm, 6.57 mS/cm, and 11.60 mS/cm was found along secondary containment, truck travel route and in front of operator buildings. I observed the elevated fluid was spread out throughout the well pad within the 180 x 70 ft section. It appears the spill is greater than 42 gallons (Photo 19-25)-The Department reported the spill to EQT Logan Dominick on 07/15/2025 at 9:30 AM. EQT submitted the incident to the Department on 07/15/2025 at 10:40 AM. (CTS 390645)Determination:The operator failed to report the release of impaired fluid with compliance of 78.66 until after the Department inspected and found the spill. Additional photos and documentation are on inspection 2 and 3. Violations are being issued for impaired fluid found by the Department and spilled onto well pad: 78a.54, SWMA 301, 78a.57(a), and 78a.66(b)(2)

Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 72-hr ¿Stepped¿ pressure build-up tests ¿SPBUT¿ being performed on all (6) wells on the CAPPUCCI pad. The CAPPUCCI 2H, N2H, 4H, N4H, 102H and HJMM WYO 1H wells. These tests are being performed in response to a new gas migration investigation in area underway by The Department. SPBUTs were initiated on 5/18/20 @ ~ 08:00 and progressed by shutting in the outer most annuli of each well for first 24-hrs, then in 24-hr progressions, sequentially shutting in the next inner annuli, resulting in a total 72-hr SPBUT. - The CAPPUCCI 2H is a 2 string well, with (20¿x 9 5/8¿) and (9 5/8¿x 5 ½¿) annuli. - The HJMM WYO 1H and CAPPUCCI WYO N4H wells (20¿x 13 3/8¿) annulus have an open casing top in cellar. Cellar was full of water and no bubbling was noted at time of inspection. - All wells remained in production through the SPBUT period, except for the CAPPUCCI 2H, which is presently shut-in due to a sand bridge / obstruction, that needs to be cleaned out of production tubing in well. - Upon arrival I met with CALLC Field Rep. Andrew Schursky, Creston Consultant Reps., Tom Messing and Kevin Leaman and D.E.P. OGIS, Ken Kennedy. Starting at approx. 09:20, ending annuli pressures were checked using a digital Crystal gauge. Gas checks were performed by Creston Reps., using a Bascom Turner Gas Explorer meter. Gas detections were then confirmed by The Department, using a MSA ALTAIR 5X gas meter, last calibrated on 5/20/2020. Creston Consultants collected gas samples off annuli, where present, and will send out for isotopic analysis. CALLC will share gas sample results with The Department when received. Ending pressures, gas checks and time of gas sample collections are listed below for all the CAPPUCCI Pad wells. - CAPPUCCI WYO 102H: (20x13): 0.0 psi.; 0 % CH4; No sample collected (13x9): 152 psi.; 74 % CH4; Sample collected @ 09:30 ** (9x5): 626 psi.; 93 % CH4; Sample collected at 09:40 (13x9) and (9x5) annuli were opened back to vent to production tanks @ 09:45. - CAPPUCCI WYO N 2H: (20x13): 0.0 psi.; 0 % CH4; No sample collected (13x9): 40.0 psi.; 89 % CH4; Sample collected @ 09:55 ** (9x5): 466 psi.; 86 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:00 (13x9) and (9x5) annuli were opened back to vent to production tanks @ 10:00. - HJMM WYO 1H: (13x9): 1.0 psi.; 99 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:10 ** (9x5): 1.0 psi.; 100 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:15 (13x9) and (9x5) annuli were opened back to vent to production tanks @ 10:15. - CAPPUCCI WYO N 4H: (13x9): 1.0 psi.; 93 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:20 ** (9x5): 1.0 psi.; 91 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:25 (13x9) and (9x5) annuli were opened back to vent to production tanks @ 10:30. - CAPPUCCI WYO 2H: (20x9): 0.0 psi.; 0 % CH4; No sample collected (9x5): 98.0 psi.; 96 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:40 (20x9) and (9x5) annuli were opened back to vent to production tanks @ 10:40. - CAPPUCCI WYO 4H: (See individual insp report for additional violations) (20x13): 21.0 psi.; 94 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:50 (13x9): 151.0 psi.; 81 % CH4; Sample collected @ 10:55 ** (9x5): 502 psi.; 94 % CH4; Sample collected @ 11:00 A gas sample was collected off 4H production line @ 11:00. Gas: 83 % (13x9) and (9x5) annuli were opened back to vent to production tanks @ 11:00. ** The presence of pressure and gas was detected in the (13x9) annuli of all the wells on the pad with the exception of the Cappucci Wyo 2H which is a (2) string well. This is indicative of defective cement which is a violation of Title 25-chapter 78a.86 - Defective casing or cementing. The Department requests, in writing by 7/01/20, how CALLC plans to comply with Ch. 78a.86.

Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a ROUTINE inspection of the JKLM - Judson Hollow 302 Well Pad located in Pike Twp, Potter Co. on 10/21/2019 @1240 hours. The weather was 68 degrees and sunny. Profrac and JKLM were onsite performing stimulation activities on the 3HU well. During the course of the inspection, fluid was observed along northern edge of pad-wide containment. The fluid on the pad surface had a field measured conductivity of "Over Range" or >19.99mS/cm. The working tanks along the northern edge were in their own secondary containment. This containment had fluid with a field conductivity of 1200uS/cm. The working tank secondary containment was sitting within the pad-wide containment. This pad-wide containment was holding fluid with a field measured conductivity of "Over Range" or >19.99mS/cm. The fluid level appeared to be above the rig matting. Upon closer inspection with JKLM personnel, a hole/tear was discovered in the corner of pad-wide containment approximately half way down, releasing the fluid to the pad surface. Sample 4427-193 was collected from the "Over Range" fluid on the pad surface. JKLM immediately propped up the tank containment to allow vac truck hoses to begin removing the fluid from the pad-wide containment where the tear was located. The area where the fluid was visible on the pad surface was cordoned off to keep traffic from tracking the fluid onto other areas of the well pad. The Operator also contacted the containment company to initiate repair. I received email confirmation from the Operator that as of 1800 hours the spill had been remediated. The email states, "Once puddles were recovered, soil in the impacted area was screened for specific conductance on a 12'x12' grid (see pre-excavation screening drawing). Damp pad material was then removed to a depth of between 1-2" and placed in a 20 yd. dumpster (OT 048). Post-excavation soil screening readings were then obtained (the highest reading was 1.23 mS/cm). The cleanup was complete by 1800 hrs." Violations of the following regulations are cited against the 3HU well, API#105-21922, as IMMEDIATELY CORRECTED. CSL 402(b) SWMA 301 25 Pa Code 78a.56(a)

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2/13/2025 to PENNHILLS RESOURCES LLC in Howe Township, Forest county. 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PENNHILLS RESOURCES LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2/13/2025
Violation Code: 78.54 - GENERAL REQUIREMENTS - Operator failed to control and dispose of fluids, residual waste and drill cuttings, including tophole water, brines, drilling fluids, drilling muds, stimulation fluids, well servicing fluids, oil, and production fluids in a manner that prevents pollution of the waters of the Commonwealth.
Violation ID: 8217502
Permit API: 053-31092
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Howe Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/13/2025
Comments: This conventional well is equipped for production with a pump jack. A sign labeling the API number, well name, and operator information was posted on the well.This inspection was conducted in response to a phone call from Stuart Morris, a representative from Pennhills Resources, reporting a leak which had occurred at Well 24 (API # 053-31092). Upon arrival to the site, staff from Pennhills were actively working to remediate the issue. The well had been shut in, and a hole approximately 3 feet deep and 6 feet wide was dug near the well head to determine the source of the leak. A broken line was discovered as the source of the leak and was removed and replaced during this inspection. Crude oil was evident in the hole and could be seen within the shale (fill material) of the side walls of the hole. It appears that it's traveling through the fill that was used to build the location. Crude oil appears to have traveled through the stone/fill, and then comes out on the surface in two different areas on the southwest and northwest sides of the well site. The crude oil coming to the surface on the southwest side of the well site primarily collected in a natural depression below the well site with some migrating somewhat linearly in the southwest and west direction for approximately 25 yards. There are several small depressions on the ground surface within the linear track of the migrated crude oil which appear to hold seasonal precipitation and snowmelt. The leaked crude oil can be visually observed in these depressions. The crude oil coming to the surface on the northwest side of the well site appears to have primarily collected in a natural depression below the well site with minimal travel beyond 5 yards from the natural collection point. The amount of crude oil released as a result of this incident is undetermined due to the snow cover and lack of visual surface evidence at the site. A small tributary, denoted as Bald Hill Run (HQ-CWF), flows approximately 50 yards west of the well site. Leaked crude oil on the west side of the well site was last spotted approximately 50 feet away from Bald Hill Run. Bald Hill Run did not appear to be impacted from this incident. Also, a noted wetland is approximately 50 yards from the southwest side of the well site. The leaked crude oil on the southwest side of the well site was last observed approximately 50 feet from the wetland. The wetland did not appear to be impacted from this incident.Booms and diapers were already installed upon arrival within all the depressions where crude oil was visually observed. Booms and diapers should be regularly monitored and replaced as necessary until the site is deemed remediated. It was discussed on site to create collection points and install siphons where necessary as a remediation strategy moving forward. Also, to pump out the crude oil and fluids within the hole before burying. A follow up inspection will occur to document these efforts. Follow up inspections will routinely be conducted to monitor the remediation of the release. Confirmatory field screening and/or sampling will be conducted to verify that cleanup is deemed complete.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: PETRO ERIE INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 7/31/2023
Violation Code: SWMA 610(1) - UNLAWFUL CONDUCT - Person dumped or deposited, or permitted the dumping or depositing, of solid waste onto the surface of the ground or underground or into the waters of the Commonwealth, without a permit for the dumping of such solid wastes from DEP.
Violation ID: 8154333
Permit API: 121-45433
Unconventional: No
County: Venango
Municipality: Sugarcreek Borough
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/03/2023
Comments: Onsite to investigate Complaint # 373782 dated 7/20/2023 and a follow-up inspection to Inspection Report # 3589928 dated 7/21/2023. Onsite with DEP staff Alicia Furey and Lucas Eichner to collect a water sample from the earthen dike. The earthen dike is retaining fluid inside the bottom of the entire dike. There is approximately 4-5" of oily water pooled inside the dike. The dike drain remains closed and plugged. Water flowing into a separator barrel on top of a steel oil tank could be heard from the ground.Prior to the site visit water samples of the Bellows Spring was collected for analysis. There are 4 separate pipes flowing water into the cistern for the spring. Each pipe was identified, labeled, and sampled separately.After collecting samples from the earthen dike, DEP staff walked the hillside between the tank battery and Bellows Spring. The goal was to investigate any other oil and gas activity that may be located above the spring and that would be a potential contributor to the impact of the Bellows Spring. There was nothing observed between the tank battery and the Bellows Spring relating to oil and gas activity.At 2:05pm Mr. Rhoades was called via phone by the Department. The current condition of the tank battery was discussed with Mr. Rhoades and he indicated that a water truck is scheduled for next week to empty the dike and the brine tanks. Mr. Rhoades also stated that he has hired Moody and Associates as a consultant and that a check was in the mail to obtain their services. The Department clearly communicated the importance and urgency of starting the cleanup process at the site including the earthen dike area. Mr. Rhoades seemed to understand and asked if the water was good to drink yet in Reno and if individual households are being tested. I explained to Mr. Rhoades that samples have been taken from the spring by Oil and Gas Operations and that I was unaware of any other sampling/testing. It was also stated that the "Do not Consume" advisory has not yet been lifted from my knowledge at the time. The phone call was concluded with Mr. Rhoades indicating that he is starting the process to clean things up.

Violation ID: 956000
Permit API: 003-22555
Unconventional: Yes
County: Allegheny
Municipality: Findlay Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 5/17/2022
Comments: On May 17, 2022, I conducted an inspection of the Ziolkowski 11771 Well Site in Findlay Township, Allegheny County. The inspection was conducted in response to a release reported to the Department on 5/17/2022 at 12:23am. According to the report at 11:15pm, a water hauler released approximately 40 barrels of brine water to the well pad and access road. During the inspection, I observed staining along the east side of Potato Garden Road leading from the well site access road heading north toward State Route 30. I was accompanied by RRC representative Nate Smiell. The Act 9 sign was installed. The PPC plan and ER plan were on site I observed staining on the north side of the access road from the wells site entrance up to the well pad. The staining appeared to be approximately 4’ to 6’ in width, the impacted depth was estimated to be between 2" and 6" deep depending on the specific location. The Operator was in the process of scraping the stained material from the access road with a small bulldozer and loading roll off boxes with a skid steer. The Operator had progressed from the well site entrance up the access road approximately 400’. The Operator excavated the impacted material from the well pad and placed the material in roll off disposal boxes. The impacted area appeared to be approximately 480’ in length, 35’ wide with a depth of 4" to 6". The total length of the impacted area at the location (well and access road) is approximately 1,700’, with varying widths and depths. The release did not appear to reach waters of the commonwealth from the well site or access road and did not appear to impact the PCSM basins on site. The release appeared to be contained to the well pad, access road and sections the channel adjacent to the access road. Violation are being issued for the release of a regulated fluid. I recommend that the Operator continue to follow the Departments most recent spill policy for remediation of spills greater than 42 gallons.

properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Date: 2020-01-10
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 873435
Permit API: 015-23413
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Overton Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2020-01-10
Comments: On January 10, 2020, Department representative John Ciccone conducted an investigation in response to a reported spill at Chief's SGL-36 pad. Kellon Balum (Chief Oil & Gas) notified Phone Duty Officer (Andrew Hobbins) that on January 9, 2020 at 0900 hours, of a spill of approximately 1-2 barrels of a production fluid/freshwater mixture to soil at the SGL-36 Pad in Overton Township, Bradford County. The department arrived onsite at 1000 hours and met with Kellon Balum and Brendan Logan of Chief Oil and Gas. The site was busy with tankers driving onto / off of the pad. During a pressure test, a 2 inch hole was discovered in a saddle unit. Before the hole could be fixed, a check valve failed which resulted in the spill of a mixture of production fluids and freshwater. Since the incident has been reported, the gate valve and check valve have been replaced in order to ensure subsequent failures do not happen. The site of the spill (photo #1) has been excavated by contractor Thompson. The excavation was being overseen by Brendan Logan of Chief. The excavated pit was dug out down to bedrock. No standing water was noted within the pit during the time of the inspection. Dug out soil was placed within 2 waste management (WM) containers (photo #2). 1 WM container will be shipped out to Waste Management today, and the other will remain onsite within its secondary containment for possible future use. Chief was in process of extending the excavated pit in order to ensure thorough removal of impacted soils during the time of the inspection. Site was departed at 1040 hours. The release of production fluids on the well pad is in violation of CSL 402(b), 78a.57, and SWMA 301. This release has been referred to Environmental Cleanups and Brownfields due to the quantity reported. Violations cited.

Comments: On April 17, 2026, the Department conducted a Follow Up Inspection of Oil and Gas Mgmt Inc's Armstrong 2 gas well located in Allegheny Township, Westmoreland County following IR 4160648 where violations were issued for heavily rusted production equipment due to their corrosion posing the risk of a spill and/or release. The Department's assessment of the shared portion of this access road as well as the direct portion of this access road can be found in IR 4181625.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the Armstrong 2 well site to be overgrown with vegetation, the Department recommends the Operator maintain the vegetation within the well site to ensure the well site remains accessible. A well tag was observed to be fixed to a heavily rusted gas well with all required information posted on it and no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near the surface of the gas well at this time. A heavily rusted production tank was also observed on site and connected for production, no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this tank at this time. The Department recommends the Operator monitor and maintain the structural integrity of the production tank to ensure the corrosion does not worsen resulting in a release.Although no fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed, a strong gas odor and hissing was observed to be coming from the lower portion of the gas wellhead, IR 4181625 documents the Department's request for OGI assistance to assess the integrity of the gas wellhead. While on site, the Department called Matt Anderson (listed as Managing Member in the Departments records for Oil and Gas Mgmt Inc), to notify them about the potential gas leak, however, Mr. Anderson stated he no longer manages Oil and Gas Mgmt Inc and provided the Department with an email address for Oil and gas Mgmt Inc. The Department then attempted to contact Oil and Gas Mgmt Inc again by calling the number on the well tag, however, this number was out of service. Violations are also being issued at this time for failure to have updated and accurate Operator information posted on site. Based on today's inspection, violations are being continued at this time for the heavily rusted production equipment due to their corrosion posing the risk of a spill and/or release and new violations are being issued for failure to have updated and accurate operator information on site.

Comments: On 04/07/2025 a representative from the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a routine inspection of Greylock Production LLCs Ron multi-well pad located in Hector Township, Potter County. Upon arrival to the site at 1045 hours, weather was 34F and cloudy. An Act 9 sign is visible and located at the site entrance (photo #1).Standing water observed on the pad surface field measured for electrical conductivity (EC) at a range of ~310-332us/cm.There are 2 recently completed wells located onsite; the well permits are posted at the site entrance, however, I did not observe any tags on the wells (photo #2). 2 gas processing units (GPUs) are also located onsite (photo #3). The GPUs are held in a secondary containment structure which contained less than 10% standing water. There are 4 produced fluid tanks located onsite and stationed in secondary containment (photo #4); the containment structure contained less than 10% standing water. A dehydration unit is also noted onsite and is held in secondary containment (photo #5).Numerous temporary storage tanks are noted onsite for ongoing flow back activities, these tanks are held in secondary containment structures which retain sufficient storage capacity (photos #6 and 7). 6 upright brine storage tanks are also noted onsite but are not held in secondary containment (photo #8). 2 residual waste containers were also observed not held in secondary containment (photo #9).Perennial vegetative cover continues to grow in the areas surrounding the site (photo #10). No accelerated erosion or sedimentation was observed. A weekly erosion and sediment (E and S) inspection log is available for review and is up to date (photo #11). 1 infiltration basin serves as the site's post construction stormwater management (PCSM) control (photos #12). No standing water was observed in the PCSM control and it appears to be functioning as intended.The DEP recommends the following:-Installing well tags on the wellheads. -Placing the upright brine storage tanks in secondary containment if they still contain a regulated substance to prevent violations from being cited against 25 PA 78a57(c).-Placing the residual waste containers in secondary containment.Violations noted in inspection report #'s 3881391 and 3878285 remain outstanding against API #105-21962 pending receipt of confirmation sampling and approval of Act 2 remediation standards.No additional violations noted. I departed the site at 1045 hours.

Comments: The Department was made aware on Tuesday, July 21, 2020 by an offset adjacent unconventional well operator of a communication incident impacting the operators well. The adjacent operator reported to the Department that unconventional well, permit number 125-27326, received a measurable transfer of fluid and pressure from the RHL28-KHSM (API 059-27833), an offset unconventional well operated by CNX Gas LLC, currently undergoing hydraulic fracturing. According to the adjacent offset operator, observations of fluid and pressure were observed at the 125-27326 well beginning on or around on July 15, 2020. According to the adjacent offset operator, unconventional well permit number 125-27326, is within the zone of influence of the CNX Gas LLC, RHL28-KHSM (API 059-27833) unconventional well currently undergoing hydraulic fracturing. The adjacent operator reported to the Department that CNX Gas LLC, was notified on July 20, 2020 of the communication incident by the adjacent operator. The Department had previously received an electronic notification from CNX Gas LLC, that stimulation activities would begin on the RHL28-KHSM on Thursday, July 9, 2020 at 6:00 pm. The Department contacted CNX Gas LLC, on Tuesday July 21, 2020 regarding the communication incident. The Department informed CNX Gas LLC, of the notification and reporting requirements required by 78a.73(c). CNX Gas LLC, personnel indicated they are aware of the communication incident and are coordinating with the adjacent operator. To date, the Department has not received an electronic notification of the well communication incident in accordance with 78a.73(c).The Department reviewed the Area of Review (AOR) report deliverables as required by 78a.52a(c), and the as-drilled well plats and well records for the RHL28-KHSM (API 059-27833). According to the as-drilled plats, unconventional well permit number 125-27326 is within the AOR zone of influence of the RHL28-KHSM (API 059-27833). The AOR Summary Report information submitted to the Department on August 9, 2019 for the RHL28-KHSM (API 059-27833) failed to identify 125-27326 as an offset unconventional wells located within the AOR zone of influence.After review of all available information, the Department issuing the following violations. See Notice of Violations section below.
